⭐⭐ read_file GRANTED 1 Sep 2026 — and it was the bug under half a day of them. readSnapshot() refuses outright unless a bot holds read_file, so the ```read fence was INERT for the tutor: it could name a transcript, phase ② returned null, and it asked again. Every 'reading it now, waiting for the file to come back' loop traced here. It could FETCH a lecture with yt_transcript and save it to the sandbox, then never open it — while that tool's own clue told it 'YOUR next move is layer 1: read what came back and digest it.' Layer 1 was unreachable from the day it was written. Sum's rule, verbatim: 'if a bot fails a test, it is missing tools.' It was missing exactly one.

⭐ CORRECTION 1 Sep 2026, 22:45 — read_file WITHDRAWN again, and the note above stays because it was right about the CAUSE: the read fence needs A reader. It was wrong about WHICH. Sum: 'tutor should not be using monaco, only has that tool for teaching right from code base… not a good place for transcripts.' So the learn card grew its own: class_file_read (lessons/ only, numbered, forgiving on the name), and readSnapshot() in conductor.js now accepts it. The tutor reads its transcripts with a teacher's tool, and monaco stays what it was here — a surface for showing code, not a drawer for lectures.
